observations: Single photo shows a white, dusty/dirty household dry pressing iron lying on a tiled floor.
No brand or model text is visible anywhere on the body.
The power cord shows frayed, exposed strands near the plug end, with no plug cover evident on one connector.
No indicator light, heat dial markings, or steam holes are visible; it appears to be a basic non-steam dry iron.
No video or demonstration of the iron heating or being plugged in is provided.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 only shows the iron at rest; no video or powered-on shot to confirm it heats or functions.

risks.proof: A short video of the iron plugged in, heating up, and the sole plate getting hot or steam/press test.

risks.risk: Cord insulation appears frayed/exposed near the plug, a safety hazard and possible sign of internal wiring damage.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the plug and cord ends showing intact insulation or confirming damage.
risks.if_unproven: priced as needing cord repair/replacement, lowering value

risks.risk: No brand is visible, so it could be an unbranded/generic low-end iron rather than a recognized brand.
risks.proof: Clear photo of any brand label or nameplate on the base or handle.

proof_requests: A video showing the iron plugged in and heating up (sole plate hot, indicator if any).
A close-up photo of the plug and full cord length to assess wiring safety.
A photo of any brand/model label on the iron's body or base.
response.reason: Item is clearly identifiable as a basic used dry pressing iron with no brand visible; working status is unverified and cord damage is visible, so it must be priced at the worst case matching the cheapest comparable generic dry irons.
